A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same spiked-cumulant autoencoder study. Their text, equations, figures, table, and appendices A–E are readable and support reliable matching across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original autoencoder and AMP simulations, including spike recovery, reconstruction losses, downstream classification, and supplementary analyses in Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 retains original simulations and adds results for rescaled tanh and comparisons between one and two hidden neurons.

M1.justification: The tied-weight autoencoder, reconstruction objective, and AMP procedure are retained. Appendix B already formulates matrix-valued autoencoder weights in v1; the new two-unit and rescaled-tanh experiments instantiate width and activation settings within this existing family.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic spiked-cumulant distributions with correlation exponents 2 and 3 and the same downstream classification task. The added experiments vary network configurations without introducing new data or task coverage.

E2.justification: Matched comparisons retain BO/AMP, linear autoencoders/PCA, and the same nonlinear activation families. Rescaling tanh and comparing single- and double-unit versions change configurations of existing methods, without introducing a distinct baseline algorithm.

E3.justification: Figures 1–2 replace standard tanh with tanh(x/4). Appendix E.5 adds one-versus-two-unit evaluations and measures maximum spike similarity across the two weights and their mutual alignment. Existing data-generation, optimizer, and testing procedures are retained.

E4.justification: New Appendix E.5 tests how bottleneck width affects reconstruction loss, spike recovery, and alignment between neurons. The existing finite-size, low-sample-ratio tanh, additional-activation, and correlation-exponent-3 analyses remain.

E5.justification: Matched experiments retain their run counts and standard-deviation reporting, including 30 autoencoder instances and 72 AMP seeds in Figure 1. The new width experiments use the existing 30-instance reporting practice; no new uncertainty-estimation procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: Main-text tanh curves are replaced by results for tanh(x/4), a changed configuration; the original loss comparison survives as v2 Figure 4. New Figures 9–11 report lower absolute reconstruction losses with two neurons, larger gaps relative to the corresponding linear model, and marginally reduced spike similarities.

T1.justification: Several local mathematical errors are corrected: Appendix A.3 reverses an initialization-probability inequality; B.3 repairs replica summation indices, signs, and a completion-of-square factor; B.5 restores a matrix inverse; and D.2 restores the missing square in the q-hat expression. The principal theorem statements and asymptotic characterizations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, highlighted contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: suitable nonlinear autoencoders recover structure invisible to PCA, and reconstruction loss can misalign with representation quality. The introduction sharpens the framing without changing these claims.

C2.justification: Section 5 revises its discussion of replica-symmetric agreement around the rescaled-tanh examples while retaining the unresolved standard-tanh discrepancy in Appendix E.2. Section 6 and new Appendix E.5 extend the loss-versus-representation interpretation to changes in network width.

D1.justification: Appendix E.5 documents the two-unit reconstruction, independent Gaussian initialization of both weight vectors, and settings for the width experiments. Existing optimizer, numerical-solver, hardware, and paper-code access information is retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Tabanelli et al. on computational thresholds in multimodal spiked models and distinguishes that setting from its single-view model. The introduction also more explicitly separates known nonlinear expressivity from the paper's quantitative analysis of learning.

P1.justification: The introduction and replica-symmetry discussion receive localized rewrites, Appendix E.5 is added, and wording and bibliographic details are corrected. The overall section sequence and narrative remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 receive updated tanh legends and axis ranges, and three width-comparison figures are added. The original Figure 2 is retained as v2 Figure 4, other appendix figures are renumbered, and Table 1 and several figures move within the layout.

improvement.justification: v2 repairs concrete algebraic inconsistencies and adds a useful width sensitivity analysis, improving the reliability and breadth of the supporting evidence. The standard-tanh discrepancy remains explicitly documented, so agreement for tanh(x/4) does not resolve that limitation. The core theoretical scope and conclusions remain stable.
